clue.text: Not asked to join party

parts.note: the clue describes turning up at a party uninvited and getting in anyway, said as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone left off the invitation list for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To force your way into a party without an invitation is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Mug seen thus to create blockage

indicators.note: seen in a down light, the word mug is read going upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the word mug itself
thus, in this way, points to the direction the word is seen: up

explanation.surface: Looking at a mug this way causes a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on a down entry: written upwards, the word mug reads the other way, and 'thus' supplies the direction, UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog a mechanism with something sticky is to cause a blockage in it.

clue.text: Soldier held up by locks that are ferocious

indicators.note: held means the locks hold the soldier inside them

parts.note: locks of hair are tresses

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in someone's fierce hair.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is the US soldier; in a down clue 'up' means written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigresses are female tigers, creatures known for being ferocious.

clue.text: In car, one man tours scenic coast

indicators.note: tours suggests going round and round, so the letters of car, one and man are moved about

explanation.surface: A man driving alone around a beautiful stretch of coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CAR, ONE and MAN rearrange into the answer; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Connemara is a region in the west of Ireland famed for its scenic Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Book taken by hippies seeking guru?

definitions.text: Book taken by hippies seeking guru?

parts.words: Book taken by hippies seeking guru?
parts.note: hippies seeking a guru travelled to the subcontinent, so the route they took is also the title of a novel

explanation.surface: A book carried by hippies searching for a spiritual teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is E M Forster's novel, read also as the hippie trail route to the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of E M Forster's 1924 novel, also a route taken east.

clue.text: Plenty in church service

parts.note: a church service giving thanks for plenty, the crops gathered in each autumn

explanation.surface: Lots of something in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: This autumn church service gives thanks for the gathered crops, celebrating plenty.

clue.text: Jelly-like film

parts.note: as can mean like, in the sense of 'in the manner of'
pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Something resembling jelly in a cinema film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly-like' reads as one adjective, but the hyphen splits the definition from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Initially daft idea reworked with assistance

indicators.note: reworked tells us the letters of idea are rearranged
initially means only the first letter of daft is taken

explanation.surface: A silly plan redone with some help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' scrambles idea; the surface's 'daft idea' is one phrase, but daft only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aided was done with help, or assistance.

clue.text: Cut up —- last to book a dance

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut

indicators.note: last to means the final letter of book is taken

explanation.surface: Trim things, then book a dance at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for cut, since down entries read upwards that way; the dash separates the two halves of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Man feeding dog finds nothing in drawer …

indicators.note: feeding means the man goes into the dog

parts.note: a corgi is a breed of dog
Reg is a man's name
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man feeds his dog and finds nothing in a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but is one who draws: Correggio was an Italian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Correggio was an Italian Renaissance painter, and an artist is one who draws.

clue.text: Monsieur Spy heralds a French victory

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A French gentleman who spies announces a victory for France.
explanation.walkthrough: Magenta, in northern Italy, was the site of an 1859 French and Sardinian victory over Austria, which gave its name to the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Magenta in 1859 was won by the French under Napoleon III.

clue.text: One cycling round dale regularly is a setter of puzzles

indicators.note: round means the rider wraps around the letters picked out of dale

parts.note: a person cycling is a rider

indicators.note: regularly signals taking every other letter of dale, here the first and third

explanation.surface: A cyclist going round a valley sets puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes D and L from dale, which go inside RIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who poses riddles is literally someone who sets puzzles for others to solve.

clue.text: Deputy head of state on his back, with European bug

indicators.note: lying on his back means the word is laid out the other way round

parts.note: veep is American slang for the vice-president

explanation.surface: A vice-president lying on his back alongside a European insect.
explanation.walkthrough: Veep is US slang for the vice-president; 'on his back' lays him flat the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Son grasped gardening tool — duck!

parts.note: held means grasped
a rake is a gardening tool

explanation.surface: A son picks up a rake and someone shouts a warning to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' looks like a cry to dodge, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large, colourful species of duck found on coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: Huge numbers produced by a plant

parts.note: a host is a great number of people or things

explanation.surface: Lots of something are produced by a factory or plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a shade-loving garden perennial grown for its broad leaves.

clue.text: … dog bites one young lady very conventional

indicators.note: bites means the dog holds the other letters in its mouth

parts.note: a hound is a dog
I is the Roman numeral for one
a deb, a debutante, is a young society lady

explanation.surface: A dog bites a young woman of very traditional outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hidebound is rigidly set in conventional views and resistant to change.

clue.text: Good pronunciation threatening to go out

parts.note: uttering is speaking or pronouncing words

explanation.surface: Fine speech that threatens to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: A candle flame that flickers as though about to die is said to be doing this.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of a candle flickering and about to be extinguished, as its flame wavers in its own wax.

clue.text: With false stroke almost bowled, as approaching century here?

definitions.text: With false stroke almost bowled, as approaching century here?

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the stroke is dropped

parts.note: an edge in cricket is a mishit off the edge of the bat
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman nearing a hundred is nearly out after an edged shot at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham, England, where a batsman might edge and be bowled near a century.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgbaston is the Birmingham cricket ground where such batting incidents happen in Test matches.

clue.text: Holding translation's sines wrong —- should be signs

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled letters wrap round the translation
wrong tells us the letters of sines are rearranged

parts.note: a crib is a literal translation used by students

explanation.surface: A translation spells sines where it should say signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes INSES from SINES, which holds CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe your name is to sign or write it on something.

clue.text: Take down books written in lousy English

indicators.note: written in means the books are placed inside the word for lousy

parts.note: dismal can mean poor or lousy
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Removing books composed in very poor English.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a structure is to take it down piece by piece.

clue.text: Without practice, operate device

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for operate goes round the practice

parts.note: to go is to work or operate, as a machine does
an ism is a doctrine or practice

explanation.surface: Running a gadget without having rehearsed first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking: GO surrounds ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo is an informal word for a gadget or contrivance.

clue.text: Writer's stomach held in at social event social event

definitions.note: the definition means writer is: the clue's 's stands for is

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance, a social event

indicators.note: held means the word for stomach holds the word in

parts.note: pot is short for pot belly, a stomach
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guest sucking in their stomach at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' looks like a phrase about breathing in, but IN itself is held by POT to give POINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, the writing implement that writes with a small rolling ball.

clue.text: Born into old money -that's a sign

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the money

parts.note: the lira was Italy's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Being born rich is a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Cut right through modern Indian city

indicators.note: through means the letter runs inside the city name

parts.note: Pune is the modern spelling of Poona, a city in western India

explanation.surface: Slicing straight through a contemporary Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune is to cut back branches or growth.

clue.text: Hanging is a bit embarrassing

indicators.note: a bit of means only a run of letters inside embarrassing is taken

explanation.surface: Being hanged is something of an embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry wall hanging, named after the French town.

clue.text: Various directions at start of Peter Grimes, say

parts.note: south, west, east and east are compass directions, S W E E

indicators.note: start of means just the first letter of Peter

explanation.surface: Stage directions at the opening of Britten's opera Peter Grimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter Grimes' looks like the Britten opera, but Grimes is the brutal chimney sweep in Kingsley's The Water-Babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Grimes in The Water-Babies is a chimney sweep, an example of the trade.

clue.text: Part of Shelley's work in loose-leaf form

definitions.meaning: Shelley wrote the verse drama Prometheus ..., so this is part of its title
a book whose pages are not bound together

explanation.surface: Pages of a Shelley poem kept loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-leaf pages are not held in a binding, and the word ends the title of Shelley's Prometheus drama.

clue.text: See a list for what may be taxed

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see
a table is a list of figures

explanation.surface: Consulting a schedule to find taxable goods.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are liable to value added tax, a sales levy, are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Cover beast working in health centre?

parts.note: someone working in a health centre may be a doctor, abbreviated DR
an ape is a beast

explanation.surface: Hiding an animal that works at a medical clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast working in a health centre is a doctor ape, DR APE.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape something is to cover it loosely with cloth.

clue.text: Completely foreign head of state's short drink

indicators.note: short means the president's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Salvador Allende was president of Chile
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A foreign leader's small glass of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom meaning thoroughly or utterly, so completely.
